gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a named welder (Jody Collier of Welding Tips and Tricks) ran the PrimeWeld TIG225X on a 30 A breaker and welded aluminum up to 1/4 in with no problems, nor that Tricked Tins welded 0.080 in 5052 aluminum on 110 V with the YesWelder TIG-200P ACDC PRO without tripping his breaker.
standout_why: I compared against the cited homewelder.com and woodworking-projects.com/hobby-tig-welder pages, plus the uncited metal-verdict.com and welderverdict.com pages. None of them reports any measurement. homewelder says all its figures come from maker pages (October 2026). MetalVerdict says no machine there 'has struck an arc in our hands'. WelderVerdict says it does not test. Woodworking-projects lists only approximate spec-sheet figures, plus a general line that '200A-class inverters draw 25–35A input'. ChatGPT itself said 240 V is better for thicker aluminum. So the general circuit-size point is already covered. What's new is only the model-specific first-hand reports, and those are named owner tests, not lab readings. No lab or bench measurement (clamp meter, load bank, input draw) exists for any of the five candidates that I could open.
decides: This supports the PrimeWeld TIG225X as the long-term pick for a beginner who has only a 30 A 240 V circuit, since a named welder did 1/4 in aluminum on one. It also supports the YesWelder TIG-200P ACDC PRO for a beginner on 110 V working thin aluminum (0.080 in). Neither finding separates LOTOS, AHP or ARCCAPTAIN, which have no named measurements. Under angle E the page can't rank on measured performance. It should say no independent bench measurements exist and use these two named reports only as supporting evidence.

findings.label: Breaker used and aluminum thickness welded (Jody Collier, Welding Tips and Tricks)
findings.value: 30 A breaker; aluminum up to 1/4 in, 'with no issues'
findings.source_title: PrimeWeld TIG225X Complete FAQ Guide (Weldmonger / Welding Tips and Tricks)
findings.note: Author Jody Collier, posted 2026-03-10. Quote: 'I personally ran off a 30 amp breaker up to 1/4" aluminum with no issues.' That sentence doesn't state the input voltage. The same page's general guidance is a 50 A breaker for 240 V and 20 A for 120 V, so this is below the usual 240 V recommendation. It's a first-hand use report, not an instrumented measurement. The page's other figures (40% at 225 A, about 0.100 in aluminum on 120 V) are given as typical or general guidance, not his own tests.

findings.label: Aluminum welded on 110 V and 220 V (Tricked Tins video review)
findings.value: 0.080 in 5052 aluminum on 110 V without tripping the breaker; 1/4 in 6061 aluminum on 220 V
findings.source_title: YesWelder TIG-200P ACDC PRO Review: Aluminum Welding Tests by Tricked Tins
findings.note: Posted 2026-08-26 on YesWelder's own blog (maker-hosted summary of a video I couldn't see). It gives no amperage, AC balance or frequency settings. Quotes: the machine 'did not trip his breaker during the test' on 110 V, and it had 'good penetration and a clean-looking bead' on 0.080 in 5052. At 220 V he found more heat available than he expected on 1/4 in 6061. Breaker rating not stated.

findings.label: Whether any rival or top result publishes measured figures for these welders
findings.value: None of the 4 rival pages checked reports a measurement; three say outright their figures come from maker or retailer listings or that they didn't test
findings.note: MetalVerdict: 'No machine here has struck an arc in our hands' (checked 2026-11-13). WelderVerdict (https://www.welderverdict.com/best/best-tig-welder-for-beginners/) says its editors don't test. homewelder.com (cited) says its figures are from maker pages as of October 2026. woodworking-projects.com/hobby-tig-welder (cited) lists approximate spec-sheet figures only.

unsourced: A clamp-meter or load-bank reading of actual output against the set amperage for the LOTOS TIG200ACDC, YesWelder TIG-200P ACDC PRO, AHP AlphaTIG 203Xi, PrimeWeld TIG225X and ARCCAPTAIN TIG200P AC/DC. I searched for named reviewers, labs and magazines (Pro Tool Reviews, Popular Mechanics, Garage Journal, Welding Tips and Tricks forum) and found none.

Measured input current from the wall, or the amperage at which a 20 A 120 V breaker trips while TIG welding aluminum, for any candidate. The Welding Tips and Tricks TIG225X thread (t=14803) has a poster saying 'I have not measured the working in-rush current'; everything else there is for other machines.
Duty-cycle time to thermal shutdown measured by a named tester for any candidate. Search snippets point only to unnamed affiliate roundups and buyer comments.

A clamp-meter test of the Weldpro 200A AC/DC (197 A read at a 200 A setting, 4 minutes at 200 A before thermal protection) at thebackyardmag.com. The page wouldn't open (TLS certificate error) and curl wasn't approved, so I can't confirm the figures, the reviewer or the date. It's also not one of our current candidates.
The AHP AlphaTIG 203Xi brochure's 120 V input current (I1max/I1eff). The PDF came back as compressed binary and I couldn't extract the text. Either way it's a spec figure, not a named measurement.
